avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 inducer reduces meperidine levels; MAO inhibition properties may increase serotonin syndrome risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; allow 2-week washout before or after meperidine therapy

avoid_supplements.name: Serotonin agonists (5-HTP, L-tryptophan, SAM-e)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Combined serotonergic activity increases risk of serotonin syndrome, especially with meperidine's metabolite normeperidine which has MAOI properties
avoid_supplements.action: Contraindicated; do not use together; monitor for agitation, confusion, tremor, hyperthermia if exposure occurs

avoid_supplements.name: Linezolid
avoid_supplements.mechanism: MAOI properties combined with meperidine's serotonergic effects create severe serotonin syndrome risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; select alternative analgesic

avoid_supplements.name: MAO inhibitors (phenelzine, tranylcypromine, isocarboxazid)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Meperidine has weak MAOI activity; concurrent use causes severe serotonin syndrome and hypertensive crisis
avoid_supplements.action: Contraindicated; maintain 14-day separation between discontinuation of MAOI and meperidine initiation

caution_supplements.name: Grapefruit supplement
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild CYP3A4 inhibition may increase meperidine levels slightly
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for increased opioid effects; consistent dosing recommended if continued

caution_supplements.name: Valerian root
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for excessive sedation, dizziness; counsel on fall risk

caution_supplements.name: Kava
caution_supplements.mechanism: Additive CNS depression and potential hepatotoxicity with chronic meperidine use
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for enhanced sedation; limit concurrent use duration

avoid_foods.name: High-dose tyramine-containing foods (cured meats, aged cheeses, fermented products) with concurrent MAOI-like activity
avoid_foods.mechanism: Meperidine's MAOI properties combined with tyramine can precipitate hypertensive crisis
avoid_foods.action: Advise moderate dietary tyramine intake; monitor blood pressure; educate on hypertensive crisis symptoms

caution_foods.name: Grapefruit juice
caution_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition may moderately increase meperidine concentrations
caution_foods.action: Monitor for enhanced opioid effects; consistent grapefruit consumption preferable to sporadic intake

caution_foods.name: Alcohol
caution_foods.mechanism: Additive CNS depression increases risk of respiratory depression, sedation, and impaired cognition
caution_foods.action: Advise abstinence or strict limitation; counsel on overdose risk and fall hazards

monitoring_notes: Meperidine has unique MAOI properties that create critical interaction risks, particularly with serotonergic agents—serotonin syndrome is a primary concern. Monitor for CNS depression when combined with alcohol or sedating supplements, and maintain awareness of hypertensive crisis risk with tyramine exposure.
